title: Binary digits track input-head movement
statement: Let $c$ be a configuration of a machine on a Boolean input $x$, and let $m$ be a left, stationary, or right move. Encode the input-head position using fixed-width, little-endian binary digits of width equal to the binary width of $|x|+1$. If $m$ is stationary, the digits are unchanged; if $m$ is left, they are unchanged at the left boundary and otherwise undergo fixed-width decrement; if $m$ is right, they are unchanged when the scanned input symbol is blank and the head is not at the left boundary, and otherwise undergo fixed-width increment. In every case, the resulting word exists and is exactly the fixed-width binary encoding of the input-head position after the clamped move.
